mechanism: vLLM serving-flag throughput, not agent architecture. The public artifact holding the new public ceiling (2.66, The AGI Boys #22, board-verified) is romantamrazov/arc-real-agi-solution, which changes ONLY the vLLM launch argv against a stack whose gameplay/prompt/tool policy its author states verbatim is unchanged. Four-flag gap vs our own bundles (verified against setup_commands.json in the anim bundle and the tennant fork, identical in both, and against our notebook's rewrite hook which touches only MODEL_OWNER/MODEL_SLUG/SERVED_MODEL_NAME): we lack --kv-cache-dtype fp8, --speculative-config {method:mtp,num_speculative_tokens:3}, --async-scheduling, and we run --max-model-len 65536 where they run 262144. Same wheelhouse (driessmit1/arc3-vllm-h100-wheelhouse-v3, vllm==0.19.0) and same model (foysalemonshanto/qwen3-8-27b-fp8-repacked-v1), so no wheel or model change is required. MTP-3 speculative decoding multiplies exactly the quantity our own instruments say is binding: 675/675 games die on the 7920s wall at 12.8% of design turns, ~30.7 tok/s makes that wall a fixed ~240k-token budget, 97.6-98.3% of generated tokens are hidden reasoning, and 12/12 archived games ended inside an analysis step that never emitted an action.
summary: 2026-08-31 community brief. FALSIFIER 1 BROKE: the public ceiling is 2.66, not FOYSAL's 2.23, and the artifact holding it is a four-flag vLLM serving change on our exact wheelhouse and our exact model. Board corroborates the step but not the cause: The AGI Boys went 1.51 -> 1.71 -> 2.66 on two draws (08-18/08-19) then froze at 2.66 for twelve days across eight further submissions; the flags->2.66 attribution is the author's own in-kernel comment (V-doc), not an isolated A/B. Same day our TV28 fork reached n=2 at mean 1.4900 (1.62, 1.36) against the certified floor's 1.541 (n=8, sd 0.338) -- -0.05, 0.2 sigma, two draws that decided nothing in either direction. Board surged (21 teams stepped >= +0.60 vs 2 yesterday, 27.6% of submitters gained vs 20.2%) but the median gain per draw FELL 0.23 -> 0.21 and topic 738216 records a Kaggle submission-infrastructure fault live 08-30 and resolved 08-31 02:26, so the fat tail is a released backlog, not a field capability jump. We fell #153 -> #173 of 2651 on an unchanged 2.05; teams at or above us 156 -> 175; gap to the #10 line 0.93 -> 1.12. Two instrument defects found: lb_diff cannot distinguish draws-bought from a team merge (it mis-flagged Kyutai's +18 subs, which is the rfbr->Kyutai absorption of Hippolyte Pilchen, who exited at #421), and the competitions topics CLI has never printed topic BODIES at all (ApiDiscussionTopic.content exists; the renderer drops it).
lesson: Six weeks of this campaign read 'architecture > model' as AGENT architecture and screened mechanism grafts accordingly; four independent implementations of measured mechanisms now sit below the floor they were built on (Polyphony 19.8%, BlackCat 1.47, tennant 1.93, ours 1.49). The cheapest unexploited architecture was SERVING architecture, and it was the one lever our own instruments had already predicted in advance and never priced -- the agent is out of tokens, not out of ideas, and speculative decoding buys tokens without touching the policy. Two corollaries. (1) When every diagnostic you own says one quantity is binding, audit the config that sets that quantity BEFORE building another arm that does not touch it. (2) A CLI that silently drops a field is indistinguishable from a field that is empty: the topics renderer has hidden every topic body for the life of this sweep, and one SDK pull immediately surfaced Nick Pellegrin's numbers (local 5.0-5.4% vs local 2.1% for the stock harness, both scoring 1.4% on the board) -- a harness 2.4x better locally scoring identically on the LB, which is third-party confirmation of feedback_screen_calibration_range and a hard ceiling on what any offline screen can license. This is the fifth consecutive day this sweep produced an audit-the-instrument finding; the sweep has never been validated against a known-complete fixture.
